title: Descarreaux 2008: flexion-relaxation ratio (ES L2, L5) by load and fatigue
condition: standing flexion-extension, load and fatigue main effects

quantity.name: flexion relaxation ratio (FRR)
quantity.definition: RMS EMG during the movement phase (flexion: FRRF; extension: FRRE) divided by RMS EMG during the relaxed full-flexion phase (dimensionless; EMG %MVC-normalised)

source.authors: Descarreaux M, Lafond D, Jeffrey-Gauthier R, Centomo H, Cantin V
source.sample: 20 healthy adults (9 M, 11 F) without LBP

how_to_simulate: Flexion (5 s), full-flexion hold (3 s), extension (5 s)
Hand load: none or 12 kg barbell at elbows 90 deg
Output: model ES activation RMS in flexion (or extension) phase / RMS in full flexion
protocol.notes: Surface Ag-AgCl EMG bilaterally over erector spinae at L2 and L5 levels (Merletti orientation), 900 Hz, 10-450 Hz band-pass; rectified, normalised to MVC (%MVC, LIDO dynamometer, 20 deg hip/trunk flexion). Onset/cessation of silence by visual inspection of the rectified EMG. Kinematics: Optotrak LEDs on acromion, mid iliac crest, greater trochanter, lateral knee, lateral malleolus; 'total trunk angle' (not further defined in the text). Task: 5 s flexion to maximum, 3 s hold, 5 s extension (auditory cue), arms by the side; load: 12 kg barbell with elbows flexed 90 deg and upper arms along the trunk (light plastic panel replica when unloaded); fatigue: Sorensen test to exhaustion (138 +/- 37 s). No significant effect of load or fatigue on FRR (P > 0.05). A model with zero activation in full flexion gives an infinite FRR - use a small floor or compare activation drop instead.

extraction.uncertainty: +/-0.1 (300 dpi, 44.5 px per unit); sd = error-bar length (SD vs SEM not stated)
extraction.check_notes: Two independent readings (visual at 150 dpi; pixel bar-top detection at 300 dpi) agree within 0.07 for all Fig 5 bars.

pass_rule.rule: |model - mean| <= 1 SD (angles); for SEM-reported data use SD = SEM x sqrt(n)
